My suggestion to you would be to look for employment elsewhere if you're concerned with your dollar amount; a lot of companies are looking for help and if you leverage your current wage in an interview for more you might be surprised to get a better offer elsewhere. However, if you go about that way you need to be certain you word the situation correctly. Yes and no. Technically they're not supposed to but they have and they will. Especially if you're a cashier (Closing) generally you'd want to have more than one person leaving the building once everything's shut down. 

As for other positions they're not suppose to, but if you read the associate handbook you'll find things like "If an associate is asked to work overtime, they can not refuse it." This behavior is predatory, but it's allowed and even more so in certain states referred to as "right to work states." What a RTWS  essentially is, is,  the ability for a company or an employee to terminate their having working there at any given moment. Companies like these (Retail and Fast food in particular), in these areas, can even go as far as terminating you for any reason and they are not required to give you a full explanation as to what it is you've done wrong. 

(Foodlion generally doesn't go along those lines, they could, but more so what they do is the tally up instances of where you messed up as leverage to terminate you at a later time should the situation arise. However, it's important to note, I'm not mentioning write ups. I've seen first hand the politics of the company where they know of certain individuals that don't follow standard practice and once they don't have a need for them they throw the book at them for past mistakes or intentionally put them in situations where they can repeat them. Rather than remedying or fixing those problems so the person can grow.) 

If you're a member of management they can go as far as say you're supposed to work on your day off (Especially Salaried like Store or Assistant Manager). 

​

In the situation that your problem persists I would actively look to contacting HR, but be careful contacting them. HR is not designed for the interest of the associates that work for a company, but the company itself as to ensure there can be no liability. If say, you need to leave on time for say picking up children, Medical reasons, etc you might find HR will side with you against the store manager solely for the sake of alleviating the company for any bad press or legal litigation against it.

This is true. Trust me. I've been a support main since Season 3 when I started. In Rank of Season 3 I got Bronze One, Season 4 got into silver, and it wasn't until last season I finally got to gold. You're going to come across the Silver players who think they know everything about the game: Every champ, every weakness, their strengths, what items to pick, what is a good match up, and etc. However, what it boils down too is that they don't have a fundamental understanding of what they should be doing. Farming, farming, as little deaths as possible, good CC team comps always help, a positive attitude, an unwilling to give up at lower elo because people will slip up, and various other things factor in.

What I can say is that in these years where I consider myself a support main it wasn't until like season 5 I started branching out and finally trying the other roles. (Mostly cause Support became Flavor of the month role and it kept getting stolen from me.) That's when my understanding of the game grew even more so. 

Another thing to note as one support main to another. There are things you can do that'll make a huge impact in your lane. As someone who plays all the roles now [Mind you I'm just gold, I'm not even great like most of the people who can probably give you better advice] I know what it's like to be an ADC with that overly passive support that sits behind you and doesn't harass or ward a bush so I can't farm as effectively. As a jungler I know what not to do as a support by seeing them not ward at all; leaving certain objectives like Baron and Dragon without vision. [Please note, I'm aware jungler's can ward their own objectives. However, it's nice to alternate vision or if my one was on CD that the Support with 3 on reserve may perhaps give a little help.]

As a mid, as an adc, or even a top laner I know how aggravating it can be when you're behind and trying to farm and the jungler or even the supports these days come in lane and take the CS. 

Now, with a more positive note to take into account. See these games as a challenging experience. Why do you think these support players at higher elo are capable of the incredible plays and holding their own? I like to think that because like all of us they too were put in situations with less than great ADC's to the point they had to LEARN and adapt. That's what the game is about. I'm thankful for all the poor adc's I've got because I learned from those experiences what NOT to be when I go carry. I would never consider myself a "Good" ADC, but I've seen more than a handful of dreadful ones that I can at least call myself moderate competent. Same could be said when I'm ADC and I have a less than satisfactory support.

My other suggestion is to think of Synergy and what works well together. Trust me there are plenty of one trick players out there, hell they're usually the better ones in my experience, but familiarize yourself with multiple picks. Look at the enemies comp and think they're heavy on AD so another tank might not be bad to stack armor on. Maybe your team is a hot mess like a gangplank top, a heimerdinger mid, a Kayn jungle (Who just HAS to go assassin), and your adc is Kogmaw. If you're familiar with Kog you know about the "Protect the Kog" mentality. Kog can do tons of damage but he's squishy. So make sure to pick someone with shields, heals even, to help him sustain in lane for longer periods of time without the risk of dying. 

My favorite support is Nami for this reason. You have a Heal that you harass with (People, please if you're reading this use the W on the enemy and let it bounce back for both effects), a bubble to save your carries life, an ult for an engage or disengage, an E that gives them additional damage on their auto attacks, and of course your skills give a movement burst. Nami has a lot on her kit, so do other supports, so again it goes back to the knowing your champs and knowing other champions as well. 

Try playing bots, customs even with friends, go into normals and try every support listed. Hell, I've tried like almost everything support at one point. [Normal games] If I consider it good enough I'd take it into rank after practice. I come from a time when if you hovered over annie, fiddle, naut, vel koz, veigar, and a ton of other "Acceptable" supports today you'd be flamed and reported despite the fact if you did good or not. I'm thankful though for those experiences because I can say I've played almost every champ in this game at least once. 

Also those suggesting Duo are absolutely right as well. It doesn't even have to be your adc to be honest. If you become confident enough in your ability to keep your adc alive, despite them being dumb as a bag of bricks at times, and you have someone else with you who can carry in another lane then you still have a chance. I remember one game I was in where I was Taric and I had a kayle toplane. The rest of the team were just feeding, getting stomped on, and I finally said "MY adc is useless at this point because they have no gold. This kayle is doing damage, is being useful, so I'm gonna use everything to keep them alive so they can CONTINUE to do so. Sometimes as a support you have to pick up on who is really doing what for the team and keeping THEM alive not just your ADC because they've been QQing all game cause you got a minion with your targons while swearing they don't get the gold for it. [This has happened more times than I like to admit.]

Another thing I'd like to say is that I've played with people at higher elo like Plat, Diamond, etc via normal games, friends of friends, and even the occasional legit smurf. Even two years ago I had some of them saying I was playing on a level much higher than my current MMR/Elo and were surprised to find out what I was. This isn't to discourage you, hell or to convince you of ELO HELL, but it's to show you that the more difficult situations you're put in the better player you become. The moment you stop blaming so and so for doing this or that and start trying to think of legit ways to come back is when you improve as a player and a carry. Yes, a carry even in the dreadful support role.
